deviations.description: ppi_gaps: BIONIC features of the samples
deviations.explanation: 1.6.1 takes the top `gene_add_num` (256) genes of `gene_list_sel.txt` by expression first and only then drops those without a PPI embedding, so a gene without one uses up a slot and the mean runs over fewer than 256 genes. v2 restricts the list to the genes that have an embedding before it takes the top 256. The two agree whenever every gene of the list has an embedding (variants `default` and `tpm`); with 30 of 300 genes missing they average different gene sets, and the trained parameters and the predictions downstream differ (the autoencoder embedding does not use BIONIC).
deviations.name: ppi_gaps/bionic

findings: The predictor network is the 1.6.1 network apart from docstrings and type hints, so a `state_dict` loads into both with `strict=True` and the forward pass agrees at the `forward` class in eval and in train mode. The autoencoder (encoder, decoder, loss, noise `np.random.binomial(1, 0.2)`) is also unchanged.

The v2 preset (commit 174ceea7, B5) is `dipkGeneExpression` with `gene_list: landmark_genes` plus `bionic` and `molgnet`. 1.6.1 has two defaults: the class attribute `gene_list` is `gene_expression_intersection` (2269 genes) but its `hyperparameters.yaml` sets `gene_list: landmark_genes`, which every experiment run uses; the preset follows the latter.

The v2 preprocessing (`log2(x + 1)` for linear units only, then the per-sample z-score with `ddof=1`) reproduces `load_cell_line_features`: the float32 path is exact and the float64 CSV loader agrees at the `forward` class. 1.6.1 chose the log step by the dataset name (`CCLE`, `CTRPv1`, `CTRPv2`); v2 reads the `expression_unit` of the modality and takes a source without a unit as log scale.

The autoencoder is fit on the unique training samples and validated on the unique early-stopping samples in both versions. v2 additionally moves the last training row to the validation rows when `len(train) % batch_size == 1` (`avoid_singleton_batch`), which 1.6.1 does not: there a trailing mini-batch of one row makes `BatchNorm1d` raise in training mode. The case keeps every batch larger.

BIONIC: the PPI table and the gene list are the real artifacts in both versions (replaced here by a synthetic table). The aggregation is identical when every gene of the list has an embedding; with gaps v2 and 1.6.1 average different gene sets (deviation `ppi_gaps/*`, see the explanation there).

v2 cannot read a precomputed ragged `molgnet_features` view: `Dataset.get_drug_features` goes through `_aligned_fetch`, which needs a 2-D float matrix, and raises `ValueError: setting an array element with a sequence` for the object array of per-drug tensors (the featurizer only catches `KeyError`). A `.h5mu` cannot store such a ragged `varm` entry either, so v2 always computes MolGNet from the SMILES with the `MolGNet.pt` artifact during the fit. 1.6.1 reads one `MolGNet_<drug>.csv` per drug. The case feeds the same tensors through the patched `_compute_molgnet_embedding`.

Training loop: Adam without weight decay, MSE on the squeezed outputs, the best validation epoch checkpointed and reloaded, early stop when the epochs without improvement reach `patience`, the early-stopping loader shuffled, as in 1.6.1. The seeded runs agree at the `train` class once the predictor weights are loaded (see the module docstring for why a seed alone cannot do that).

The attention key bias (`fc_k.bias`) has an exactly zero gradient (softmax is invariant to a constant shift per query), so Adam turns float32 rounding noise into full steps on it; it is not compared. The output does not depend on it.
